reuse.why: Re-writes the tolerance formula Math.round(Math.abs(amount) * 0.075) inline instead of calling the existing getApproxNumberThreshold in shared/rules.ts that the matching code uses.

duplication.why: The 7.5% tolerance is now defined twice (rules.ts and schedules.ts), so matching and planning can drift apart.

placement.why: Extending getExpectedScheduleAmount in shared/schedules.ts is the right layer, with an optional op parameter.

scope.why: Focused on the amount rule, the preview caller and tests.

maintainability.why: Only the preview path passes the op; forecast-schedules.ts, schedules/app.ts (action sync and post-transaction) still call without it, so the 'shared' rule is silently partial and the optional parameter makes forgetting it easy.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getExpectedScheduleAmount in shared/schedules.ts re-implements getApproxNumberThreshold (shared/rules.ts) instead of calling it.

disguised_duplication.where: The tolerance formula is copied nearly verbatim from getApproxNumberThreshold, not disguised.

one_place.where: The rule is in getExpectedScheduleAmount, but only computeSchedulePreviewTransactions passes amountOp; forecast-schedules.ts:97 and schedules/app.ts:156/590 still get the exact value for approximate amounts.
